column1: # P4-130 — which upstream libjpeg-turbo release each C oracle runs against.
# Every differential gate in this repository is only as current as the C
# library it compares against. Upstream shipped 3.2.0 on 2026-06-30 and it took
# two months for anyone to notice that all thirteen oracle pins still said
# 3.1.4.1 — because the version lived in thirteen shell fragments across five
# workflow files and nowhere else. This file is the single place that answers
# "which release does a green gate prove parity with?".
# `tests/oracle_version_pins.rs` enforces it in both directions: a workflow pin
# with no row here fails, and a row here that no workflow installs fails.
# `scripts/check_oracle_currency.sh` asks the remaining question — whether
# upstream has moved past `tool-current` — on a weekly schedule.
# The same gate reads every *job* in every workflow, rather than a list of
# workflow files, and holds each oracle-provisioning job to three things: it
# names the release it installs (a package manager's own name for the package
# does not), it *asserts* that release rather than printing it, and the prefix
# it checked is the prefix its tests resolve. A gate keyed to workflow names is
# how `brew install jpeg-turbo` survived in ci.yml's C Interop leg for a day
# after the aarch64 Full C Parity legs lost exactly that shape.
# Roles:
#   tool-baseline  the release the existing expectations were written against.
#                  Kept as its own leg on purpose: bumping it in place would
#                  re-baseline every expectation at once, and any divergence
#                  that hid behind the bump would be indistinguishable from a
#                  pass.
#   tool-current   current upstream stable, and therefore the parity target.
#   trace-current  current upstream stable at the *v8 ABI*, built from source.
#                  A separate row because the packaged release cannot play this
#                  part: upstream's deb ships JPEG_LIB_VERSION 62, and the
#                  classic-ABI trace suites compare against the v8 ABI the shim
#                  claims. `tests/oracle_version_pins.rs` therefore requires a
#                  `--branch` clone site for this row, not merely a version
#                  that appears somewhere.
#   submodule      references/libjpeg-turbo. Not a tool pin: it is built in CI
#                  as the *baseline* classic-ABI trace oracle
#                  (`/tmp/ljt8/prefix`, v8 ABI) and it is the source every
#                  `j*.c:NNN` citation quotes. It is one release line ahead of
#                  `tool-baseline` and one behind `trace-current`, which is the
#                  split this file exists to keep visible.
# role
tool-baseline
column3: libjpeg-turbo-official deb at /opt/libjpeg-turbo, or a source build (/usr/local on x86_64, /tmp/ljt3141/prefix on aarch64)
column5: Behaviour-regression leg: djpeg/cjpeg/jpegtran + libturbojpeg for the differential suites, at the release the current expectations were written against. The aarch64 legs — Full C Parity and ci.yml's C Interop — build it from source: homebrew has no per-version jpeg-turbo formula, so brew install measured whatever the packager shipped that week.

column1: tool-current
column3: libjpeg-turbo-official deb at /opt/libjpeg-turbo, or a source build at /tmp/ljt320/prefix on aarch64 (upstream ships no macOS package)
column5: Current-parity leg: the same differential suites against current upstream stable, selected explicitly through LIBJPEG_TURBO_PREFIX rather than PATH order. Covers the root matrix, the C-ABI crate's TurboJPEG and stock-tool suites, and the weekly exhaustive full-c-parity matrices on x86_64 and aarch64.

column1: trace-current
column3: source clone built with WITH_JPEG8=1 at /tmp/ljt320v8/prefix
column5: Current-parity leg for the classic-ABI trace suites, which compile a C oracle and compare traces line by line at the v8 ABI. Built from source because the deb above is JPEG_LIB_VERSION 62.

column1: submodule
column5: Classic-ABI trace oracle built with WITH_JPEG8=1, and the source tree the C citations quote. Already on the 3.2 line, which is why the tool pins and the citations disagreed unnoticed.
